subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or wait for the broader per-session policy design to define cron enforcement and precedence?
rationale: This creates or reuses a public config surface and defines a hard scheduled-tool security boundary, so automation should not choose the precedence or default guarantee.

options.title: Design Cron Policy In Session Model
options.body: Use the broader per-session/capability-policy direction to define cron precedence first, then add one canonical cron enforcement path with docs and tests.

options.title: Add Dedicated Cron Scope Now
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.*` as a narrow global cron policy with explicit deny precedence over per-job allowlists and delivery behavior.

options.title: Document Per-Job Tools Only
options.body: Decline a global cron policy and make per-job `toolsAllow` plus announce-delivery safeguards the supported operator workflow.

recommendation.title: Design Cron Policy In Session Model
recommendation.body: Use the broader per-session/capability-policy direction to define cron precedence first, then add one canonical cron enforcement path with docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and is the best visible routing candidate for the config/security-boundary choice.
